articles.headline: On July 15, an Indian Professional Posted to Britain Stops Paying Twice for the Same Pension

vision_image_match.what_photo_shows: London skyline with trees and buildings in foreground
vision_image_match.reason: The photo shows the City of London, which is relevant to a story about an India-UK trade pact and professional mobility.

diaspora_angle.note: The article directly addresses the impact of the trade deal on Indian professionals and NRIs, particularly regarding pension contributions and temporary work routes. The 'diaspora weary of shifting visa goalposts' line is a strong, natural connection.

factual_flags: The article states 'The Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement — CETA, the formal name for the free-trade agreement the two countries signed in July 2025 — comes into force on Wednesday, July 15'. However, the headline states 'On July 15, an Indian Professional Posted to Britain Stops Paying Twice for the Same Pension', implying July 15, 2024. If the agreement was signed in July 2025, it cannot come into force on July 15, 2024. This is a significant date discrepancy.
suggestions: Clarify the exact year for the CETA signing and implementation dates to resolve the factual contradiction.
